questions.question: A custom derivative is linear in its tangent and returns finite values. What additional evidence is necessary before calling it exact?
options: Agreement with the actual primal derivative through an independent derivation or numerical check.
A larger batch size so its bars look smoother.
No additional evidence: linearity guarantees the coefficient is correct.
questions.explanation: Linearity is necessary, but a wrong constant multiple of the true derivative is also linear and finite. Independent comparisons establish the missing mathematical agreement.
